lines: The train lurches forward. Through the window, the darkness gradually gives way to grey twilight...
Hours pass. The first real sunlight you've seen in days breaks through the clouds.
MERIDIAN CITY — TERMINUS. Please watch the gap.
You step onto the platform. The station is vast — vaulted ceilings, holographic advertisements, crowds of people moving with purpose. After the isolation of the frontier, it's almost overwhelming.
— MERIDIAN CITY DIRECTORY —
WEST CORRIDOR: Workshop District — Crafting, Engineering, Repairs
EAST CORRIDOR: Civic Center — Government, Land Registry, Administration
NORTH-WEST WAITING ROOM: Connects to Market Quarter (via Civic Center)
NORTH-EAST WAITING ROOM: Information Office
SOUTH: Return to Train Platform

WEST CORRIDOR: Workshop District — Crafting, Engineering, Repairs
EAST CORRIDOR: Civic Center — Government, Land Registry, Administration
NORTH-WEST WAITING ROOM: Connects to Market Quarter (via Civic Center)
NORTH-EAST WAITING ROOM: Information Office
SOUTH: Return to Train Platform
Calloway frowns. 'Halden? Yeah, I know him. Transit courier, ran the evening manifests. Quiet kid, kept his head down.'
'Hasn't been at his post in days. Last time I saw him, he was in the Market Quarter — acting jumpy, looking over his shoulder.'
'Left his logbook on the platform bench. I put it aside, but he never came back. It probably got swept into the market during the evening rush.'

actions.text: A holographic advertisement cycles nearby: 'MERIDIAN-7 — Powering Progress. Visit the Array Hub for premium services.'

lines: Meridian Station feels different. The Array's holographic advertisements are dark — blank panels where 'MERIDIAN-7 — Powering Progress' used to cycle.
The trains are running, but on backup power. The overhead lights flicker slightly at regular intervals. A hand-lettered notice board has replaced the electronic departures display.
Calloway is behind the window as always. Some things survive every ending.

The station directory board has been updated. New routes are listed below the familiar city corridors: 'UNDERLUMEN TRANSIT — BIOLUMINESCENT PASSAGE (PERMIT REQUIRED)' and 'ARRAY TRANSIT HUB — SHARED SERVICES TERMINAL.'
Three different logos share space on the departure board. Someone has drawn a small, careful symbol connecting all three — a circle, a crystal lattice, and an organic spiral.

The platform crowds include people you've never seen here before: Unbounded guides with bioluminescent markers on their gear, Array technicians in white, Ring citizens looking at all of it with cautious curiosity.
A new checkpoint stands at the station entrance — Ring Authority officers checking transit passes, logging arrivals. The process is efficient. The queue is short.
The Array's advertisements are still running, but the branding has changed: 'MERIDIAN-7 — RING-ADMINISTERED INFRASTRUCTURE. SERVING THE PEOPLE OF THE TERMINATOR ZONE.'
The trains run on schedule. The lights are steady. Control, it turns out, looks a lot like before — just with different insignia on the walls.

options.description: Energy drain zones. 4-5 floors. Cost: 20 silicon. Requires Tier 2 cleared + automation level 3.

actions.text: You step away from the expedition board.
You already have an active expedition. Complete or abandon it before starting another.

lines: The expedition board is dark. A notice reads: 'NIGHTSIDE BREACH OPERATIONS — AUTHORIZATION REQUIRED.'
'Expeditions into the Nightside perimeter are classified operations. Authorization requires a formal faction mandate from the Civic Council.'
The Council has not yet reached a decision on the Lightkeeper mandate. The path forward isn't clear yet.
